card: Bitcoin Core cannot currently detect when an operating system lacks global IPv4 or IPv6 routing, causing nodes on IPv4-only hosts to waste feeler and outbound connection attempts and AddrMan capacity on unreachable IPv6 peers. This PR introduces periodic reachability checks via UDP route lookups without transmitting packets, dynamically marking IPv4 or IPv6 as unreachable if no global route exists while the other network remains up. Networks marked unreachable are excluded from automatic outbound connections and new AddrMan additions until connectivity is restored. The author notes that IPv6 unreachability is common and causes ongoing futile connection attempts across many node environments.
changed_since_previous: Now has a concrete diff; the implemented logic and commits match the approach described in the previous version.
evidence: PR description: "In many network environments, IPv6 peers cannot be reached, which is currently not detected. As a result, IPv6 addresses take up spots in AddrMan, and we make futile attempts to connect to them (e.g. feelers or network-specific connections)."
problem: Nodes running in environments without IPv6 connectivity (or IPv6-only environments) cannot detect the missing route. As a result, they continuously make futile outbound and feeler connection attempts to unreachable peers and occupy AddrMan slots with addresses they cannot reach.

risk.why: A false positive in route detection would disable automatic outbound connections and address relay for an entire IP family on affected nodes.

scope_notes: The implementation relies on OS-specific error codes and routing table behavior when connecting unbound UDP sockets across Linux, Windows, and BSDs without sending packets over the wire. Automated functional or unit tests are not yet included in the PR.
summary: Adds automatic detection of IPv4 and IPv6 internet reachability using OS route lookups via UDP connect() calls to well-known unicast IP addresses without sending packets. If only one address family has a usable route, the other is dynamically removed from g_reachable_nets and added back if connectivity is restored. The check executes one minute after startup and every ten minutes thereafter, but is skipped if -onlynet is specified, if the network uses a proxy, or if automatic outbound connections are disabled.
